- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥ 3 consecutive negative values), reduce forecasted peaks and avoid over-optimistic upward trends.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecasted highs at 1–2% below the peak or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 standard deviations.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive signals (e.g., 0.27 or higher), model often overreacts — dampen forecast growth by 10–20% in the next 5–7 days.  
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion — if recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive downward moves), forecast should not exceed 1–1.5σ above recent low.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 unit per day until trend stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit recent volatility — smooth out forecast curves using 3–5 day moving average or apply 10% dampening to volatility spikes.
